function: Multi-agent TD3 learns AP beam codebooks and RIS reflection (phase-shift) codebooks for initial access from received-power feedback, without CSI (p. 1, 6).
system: Cell-free mmWave MISO: 4 APs with 32 antennas, 4 passive reflecting RISs of 32 or 256 elements with 3-bit phases, single-antenna UEs, 60 GHz (p. 3, 11).
method: Multi-agent TD3 reinforcement learning, one agent per K-means UE cluster, bi-level reward; transfer of actor-critic weights from the first RIS to the others (p. 7, 10).
data_channel: DeepMIMO dataset, outdoor scenario O1_60 at 60 GHz, 5 paths, 16,000 UEs, used to simulate the wireless system for learning and evaluation (p. 11).
test_conditions: Same O1_60 scenario throughout, no held-out split stated; weights transferred from the first RIS to three other RISs and from 32 to 256 elements (p. 10-11).
baselines: Non-learned only: SVD beamforming with perfect CSI, DFT codebook, oversampled DFT codebook; no learned baseline, only variants with and without transfer learning (p. 10-12).
metrics: Average beamforming gain, CDF of achievable rate per UE, beam training overhead in time slots, beamforming gain per consumed power, learning iterations (p. 11-13).
q1_support: p. 11: "from the DeepMIMO dataset [36]": the outdoor scenario O1_60 at 60 GHz generates the channels G, h, and H used by the agents. The Saleh-Valenzuela model of Eq. (1) (p. 3) is only the system model.
q2_support: p. 11: "transfer learning applied to the remaining RISs results in a much faster learning process" (about 10^4 against 6 x 10^4 iterations for the first RIS); p. 11: "we transfer the knowledge gained from the small RISs (NRIS = 32) to the large RISs (NRIS = 256)".
q3_support: p. 10: "we benchmark the proposed MA-DRL approach with the DFT-based codebook", plus SVD and O-DFT (Figs. 5-6): all non-learned. No earlier learned codebook method or standard DRL (DDPG, DQN, PPO) is run; Fig. 4 only compares variants with and without transfer learning, on convergence.
q4_support: p. 12: "the beam training overhead of the DRL solution is in the order" of R x F^r + M_AP x A^m (p. 13), which is signaling overhead (beams swept, Table I, p. 11) and does not count; p. 11 gives iterations to converge only. No FLOPs, parameters, or runtime of the agents.
q5_support: p. 3: "Using the publicly-available DeepMIMO dataset [36]"; p. 11: scenario O1_60 of DeepMIMO is the dataset for learning and evaluation. The paper releases no code and gives no link of its own.
notes: Title on page 1 is 'Multi-Agent DRL for Distributed Codebook Design in RIS-Aided Cell-Free Massive MIMO Networks' with DOI 10.1109/TCOMM.2024.3483041, so the PDF matches. Area 3: the learned part designs AP beam codebooks and RIS reflection codebooks; K-means clustering and the AP and RIS selection of Algorithm 2 (p. 8) are not learned beamforming. q2 counts the reported transfer learning to other RISs (other sites) and to the 256-element RIS (p. 10-11) under the transfer clause of the rule; the reviewer may confirm. q4 stays 0: the iterations to converge (p. 11) and the beam training overhead of Table I (p. 11) are not computational cost. Table I was read from the page image. The paper selects rows 1401 to 1700 with 80 UEs per row but states 16,000 UEs (p. 11).
